title: Replacing a date with an invalid date writes non-date bytes
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img, desktop route. USE EDGE; REPLACE WHEN WITH CTOD("02/30/92"); DISPLAY ID,WHEN; USE; USE EDGE. Stop the guest and extract EDGE.DBF with mcopy.
observed: Record 1 WHEN becomes the eight ASCII bytes ,)/-1124 (hex 2c292f2d31313234), rather than eight blanks. DISPLAY shows 11/24/00. The invalid bytes survive closing and reopening. This is a persistence defect beyond earlier audit L045, which described display of empty/invalid dates.
expected: A blank/invalid CTOD result must leave a valid blank date representation. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/dbf.md, section 5: D fields contain YYYYMMDD or blanks. This corrupts the field representation even though the table remains openable.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1654 converts every XB_D through ymd_from_jdn, including the zero/blank sentinel; only XB_U takes the blank branch at line 1675.

title: Escape and Ctrl-C cannot stop a running loop
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img, desktop route. DO LOOP. Wait 2 seconds; press Esc, wait 2 seconds; Ctrl-C, wait 2 seconds; type ? "RECOVERED" and Enter; wait 2 seconds. LOOP.PRG installs ON ESCAPE and runs DO WHILE .T. incrementing N.
observed: The screen remains at . DO LOOP; no trap output, prompt, or recovery command appears. QMP remains responsive and reports running, HLT=0. Only stopping this audit QEMU ended the session. This is failure to interrupt a program, not a claim that the infinite loop should terminate by itself.
expected: A user must be able to interrupt a mistaken loop without destroying the session. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md, ON ESCAPE/SET ESCAPE discussion. The shipped quick reference openly calls the trap inert; that documents the limitation but does not make an uncancellable loop dependable.

title: Desktop-launched status mode prints ANSI control sequences
steps: Boot flair_tenants_interactive.img with rich-fixture.img, press Ctrl+Alt+backslash, USE CLIENTS, SET STATUS ON, then ? 2+2. Allow output to settle. SET STATUS OFF restores ordinary command output.
observed: Escape sequences such as [23;1H and [0;7m fill and scroll the screen instead of positioning a status bar. The same setting works through tracer_boot.img and SAMIR.COM, so this is specific to the desktop route, not the old unrecognized SET STATUS command.
expected: SET STATUS ON should draw the status bar. Shipped quick reference qr-set.tex documents "The status bar" for STATUS; the real III+ status layout is described in dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/assist-ui-and-editors.md section 10. The DOS-route screenshot is the control.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:566 and :607 bind the status display to ANSI sequences; the DOS boot logs ANSI-WIRED/ANSI.SYS, whereas the tested desktop boot does not.

title: A successful memo replacement reads as empty until USE reopens the table
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EDGE; ? MEMO; REPLACE MEMO WITH "changed memo"; ? MEMO,LEN(MEMO); GO 2; GO 1; ? MEMO; USE; USE EDGE; ? MEMO,LEN(MEMO). Repeat with "again".
observed: Immediately after each successful REPLACE, the memo is empty and LEN is 0, even after moving away and back. Closing/reopening returns "changed memo" with length 12, then "again" on the second cycle. DBF pointers and DBT appended text are persisted correctly.
expected: Reads in the same work area should immediately reflect a successful write. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md, REPLACE; dbt.md section 4 describes the memo pointer. The read-after-write requirement is also my data-consistency expectation.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:63 retains the open memo handle, while os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1763 opens a separate writable handle and appends through it; the existing reader is not refreshed.

title: An asterisk-filled numeric overflow is presented as zero
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EDGE; REPLACE SMALL WITH 99999; DISPLAY ID,SMALL. Close/reopen EDGE and display again; extract the stopped DBF.
observed: SMALL N(4,1) is stored as **** at record offset 290, but DISPLAY prints 0.0. The same false zero appears after reopening.
expected: Preserve an unmistakable overflow indication in listings instead of presenting an ordinary zero. The storage rule is in shipped Volume One u5-entries-b.tex:577: "A number too large for its field is stored as asterisks." The expectation that the listing must not conceal that failure is my usability/data-integrity judgment; I did not run a live III+ overflow listing.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/fs/dbf.c:847 parses all-asterisk N fields with dec_parse and explicitly falls back to 0.0.

title: TRANSFORM reports overflow for a decimal value that fits its picture
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: ? TRANSFORM(123.4,"999.99"). Compare ? STR(123.4,6,2) and the adjacent decimal cases in transform.json.
observed: The six-character picture produces ***.** for 123.4, despite room for 123.40.
expected: The three integer and two fractional digit positions should produce 123.40. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/picture-function-templates.md section 3 and its 9,999.99 example; the arithmetic fit of this exact case is independently obvious.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/core/fn_builtins.c:1580 passes the count of digit slots to dec_format as the total width, omitting space for the decimal point.

title: INDEX ON cannot create an index for an empty table
steps: Fresh rich-fixture.img: USE EMPTY; INDEX ON NAME TO ZERO; SEEK "NONE".
observed: INDEX returns 29 File is not accessible. No ZERO.NDX is created. SEEK then returns 26 Database is not indexed. EMPTY.DBF is a valid zero-record table with NAME C(12).
expected: Create a valid empty index that can receive future appends. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md, empty-root layout, and commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md, INDEX. This is a common new-table workflow.
source_guess: Guess: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1124 infers key width from the current evaluated value, which is empty when there is no record.

title: Four-letter command abbreviations are rejected
steps: USE CLIENTS. Enter DISP; REPL NAME WITH "TEST"; APPE BLANK; LOCA FOR BAL>1000; SELE 2; INDE ON NAME TO TEST; STOR 5 TO X.
observed: Every abbreviation returns 16 *** Unrecognized command verb. Full spellings work for the corresponding implemented commands.
expected: Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/runtime/interpreter-and-execution-model.md:188-224 documents first-four-letter recognition. The shipped Volume One u2-commands.tex:26 explicitly instructs full spellings, so this is a historical feature gap, not an undocumented manual contradiction.

title: DISPLAY STATUS is parsed as a field expression
observed: 12 Variable not found is returned; no environment/work-area report is shown.
expected: Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/navigation-query-display.md:713-727 specifies open files and system parameters. This is separate from the fixed command SET STATUS and the old DISPLAY STRUCTURE gap.

title: DISPLAY MEMORY is parsed as a field expression
observed: 12 Variable not found is returned; no memory-variable listing is shown.
expected: Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/navigation-query-display.md:731-743 specifies names, types, sizes, scopes and values of memory variables.

title: MODIFY STRUCTURE is unavailable
observed: 16 *** Unrecognized command verb. No field editor opens, so rename/widen/narrow/add/delete with existing data cannot be reached.
expected: Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md section 2 and full-screen/assist-ui-and-editors.md section 6. Earlier K08 covers CREATE and record editors, not this reached modification command.

title: QUIT inside a PRG is rejected rather than exiting
steps: Run DO QUITPRG using rich-fixture.img. The file prints BEFORE QUIT, executes QUIT, and would then print AFTER QUIT.
observed: BEFORE QUIT is followed by 16 *** Unrecognized command verb and a dot prompt. The database process remains alive; AFTER QUIT is not run because the program aborted.
expected: QUIT should close files and end the database session when executed by a program. Named reference: dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md, QUIT; shipped Quick Reference qr-commands.tex entry QUIT says "Closes all files and leaves InitechBase".
